deep.reconstruction:
Context: an observing journal of the Göttingen observatory, Thursday 30 April 1819. The previous page ends with that morning's level ('Libelle') readings, giving the reduced value 3'21"94. The instrument is evidently the new meridian circle, read with a circle and microscopes, whose division and screw errors were studied on the previous page. The page reduces transits and circle readings of Aldebaran, Procyon and Pollux. The aims are (a) the clock correction and (b) mean declinations of Procyon and Pollux for the catalogue epoch.

(1) Aldebaran, noted as 'nicht sonderl.(?) gute Beob.', i.e. not a particularly good observation.
- Transit times over three wires: 4h25m23.0s, 25m39.3s, 25m56.4s.
- Their mean is (23.0+39.3+56.4)/3 = 39.567s, so T = 4h25m39.57s (clock time).
- Circle reading: 35°27'30". Microscope readings: 2'11"6 (first digit overwritten) and 1'53"2.
- Meteorology: barometer 27 Paris inches 5.8 lines, thermometer 13.0°.
- Tabular right ascension: α = 4h25m28.13s. Hence the clock is ahead ('Uhr voraus') by ΔT = 39.57 − 28.13 = 11.43s, more precisely 11.437s.
- Note: 'At 5½h the clock was held back 11.5s and its (daily) rate retarded by 1.5s.' This makes the clock nearly correct for the later stars.

(2) 'Aldebaran Declination': reduction from mean place to apparent place in declination, tabulated at 10-day intervals.
- The columns are: annual aberration; lunar nutation (Nut. l.); solar nutation (Nut. Sol.); precession (Pr. b. 1819).
- The last column is Σ = apparent − mean, e.g. Apr 30: −3.76+5.10−0.09−5.26 = −4.01.
- The precession column runs linearly at about 0.21" per 10 days (about 7.7"/yr ≈ 20" cos α). Extrapolated, it vanishes near 1820.0. So the reference epoch actually used appears to be 1820.0, the beginning of 1820, even though the entries are labelled '1819'.

(3) Procyon and Pollux transits and circle readings.
- Procyon: wires 7h29m29.2s, 29m45.3s, 30m1.6s. Mean = 136.1/3 → 7h29m45.367s. Circle reading 45°53'45"6, microscopes 3'58"8 and 3'36"8 (a first value 3'36"8 struck out).
- Pollux: wires 7h33m51.1s, 34m9.4s, 34m28.1s. Mean = 208.6/3 → 7h34m9.533s. Circle reading 23°7'45"3, microscopes 2'57"2 and 2'36"2.
- Meteorology: barometer 27z 5.3l, thermometer +12.9°.
- Apparent right ascensions for Apr 30.52:
  - Procyon: 7h29m45.291s + 0.536s = 45.827s.
  - Pollux: 7h34m8.940s + 0.671s = 9.611s.
- Observed minus computed: Procyon 45.367 − 45.827 = −0.46s; Pollux 9.533 − 9.611 = −0.08s.
- Mean clock correction: (−0.46 − 0.08)/2 = −0.27s ('Mittel −0"27').

(4) Declinations.
- Corrected circle readings: Procyon 45°53'46.25", Pollux 23°7'46.06". These are slightly different from the raw readings (+0.65" and +0.76"). The adjustment is presumably the division/screw correction from the previous page; this is my inference.
- Subtract the zenith point from the level, 3'21.94" (my identification):
  - Procyon: 45°53'46.25" − 3'21.94" = 45°50'24.31".
  - Pollux: 23°7'46.06" − 3'21.94" = 23°4'24.12".
- Add refraction: Procyon +57.60" → z = 45°51'21.91"; Pollux +23.87" → z = 23°4'47.99". These values are consistent with about 58" tan z scaled by the barometer and thermometer readings.
- Both stars culminate south of the zenith, so δ = φ − z with the adopted value 51°32'18.70":
  - Procyon: δ_app = 5°40'56.79".
  - Pollux: δ_app = 28°27'30.71".
- Subtract Σ to get the mean place ('D.1819'):
  - Procyon: −10.56" → 5°40'46.23".
  - Pollux: −9.73" → 28°27'20.98".

(5) 'Procyon Declin.': the same four-column reduction table for Procyon, April 30 to May 30. The Apr 30 entry Σ = −4.38+8.66+0.49+5.79 = +10.56 is the value used in (4).
errors: Aldebaran clock error: 39.567 − 28.13 = 11.437, so 11.44 would be the rounded value; Gauss writes 11.43, which is negligible truncation.

Pollux: the reduction applied, −9.73", does not agree with the Pollux reduction table on the next page. That table gives Σ = +17.64 for April 30 (2.83/3.25 aberration, about 8.70 lunar nutation, about 0.26 solar nutation, about 5.43 precession). My own estimate of the aberration (+3.25) confirms the next page. So the mean declination 28°27'20.98" appears to be about 7.9" too large, unless 9.73 came from an earlier, provisional computation.

The precession column labelled 'Pr. b. 1819' behaves as precession referred to 1820.0, not 1819.0. Its signs and zero-crossing imply this for all three stars. This is a labelling issue rather than a computational error.

The adopted value 51°32'18.70" differs by about 30" from Gauss's later Göttingen latitude (51°31'48"). It is probably a provisional instrumental constant (equator/zenith point not yet fully determined) rather than a true latitude.

results.what: Clock correction from meridian transits: mean of wire times compared with tabular right ascension
Mean-to-apparent reduction in declination via aberration, lunar and solar nutation, and precession, tabulated at 10-day intervals
Declination from circle reading: zenith-point (level) correction, refraction, δ = φ − z, then reduction to mean epoch

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine observatory reduction work: transit means, clock error, aberration/nutation/precession sums and refraction. It is of interest only as documentation of Gauss's early work with the new Göttingen meridian circle in 1819.

checkable.asserts: Procyon mean of 29.2, 45.3, 61.6 = 45.367 (third wire must be 30m1.6s)
apparent RAs 45.827 and 9.611; O−C −0.46 and −0.08; mean −0.27
δ = φ − z for Procyon and Pollux (both differences 0)
Pollux aberration in declination on Apr 30 is about +3.25", supporting the next page's Σ = 17.64 against the 9.73 used here

transcription_corrections: Procyon third wire: '28'1"6' should be 30'1"6, as required by the mean 45.367.
Pollux third wire: '38.28.1' should be 34'28"1, as required by the mean 9.533.
Aldebaran remark: 'nicht ordentl.' is more likely 'nicht sonderl. gute Beob.'
'Fr. obs.' is probably 'Uhr obs.' or 'Beob.', i.e. the observed clock time (uncertain).
Procyon declination table, Apr 30 aberration: '−4"38' is overwritten; the value used is −4.38, consistent with the sum 10.56.
